title: 🛡️ 'CrowdStrike' in Talks to Acquire 'Zscaler' — a $265 Billion Cybersecurity Deal!
body: 🛡️ 'CrowdStrike' in Talks to Acquire 'Zscaler' — a $265 Billion Cybersecurity Deal!

Cybersecurity company "CrowdStrike" is in talks to acquire its rival "Zscaler", in a deal that could become one of the biggest cybersecurity deals in history, with a combined market value of about $265 billion. Informed sources confirmed the talks are underway and an agreement could come soon, but there is no certainty they will lead to a deal.

Shares moved immediately as the news spread: "Zscaler" shares jumped about 17% in after-hours trading on Friday, while "CrowdStrike" shares fell about 8.5%. "Zscaler"'s market value is about $32 billion, while the deal is likely to be mostly in stock, because "CrowdStrike" holds only about $5 billion in cash on its balance sheet.

Any deal needs the approval of "Zscaler" CEO Jay Chaudhry, who is also the company's largest individual shareholder. "CrowdStrike" declined to comment on the reports, while "Zscaler" did not immediately respond to requests for comment. "CrowdStrike" is scheduled to report third-quarter results on December 1, and "Zscaler" first-quarter results on December 2.
Simply put: an acquisition means one company buys another company entirely, and here the two biggest companies protecting businesses from cyberattacks could merge into one giant entity.
